newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Spain labour reform proposals.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Spain labour reform proposals.

text.p: Employers and unions presented an accord on Wednesday to reduce Spain's unemployment rate of just under 22 percent, the highest in Europe. The presentation of the draft accord had been anticipated for several days. Following are economists comments:
ANTONIO VILLARROYA, MERRILL LYNCH ECONOMIST, MADRID

- "The labour reform is good particularly because it means a liberalisation of the labour market, but it hasn't gone to the root...The reform will not avoid the rigidities of the Spanish labour market. It will not make our unemployment rate fall. The impact will be minor. The effect on the markets will be moderately optimistic"
CRAIG SHUTE, FIXED-INCOME ANALYST, BEAR STEARNS, LONDON
- "The package falls short of the liberalisation employers would have liked to have seen. It also falls short of more optimistic market forecasts."

"But it is a step forward in reforming Spain's relatively rigid market. It modestly lowers the cost of shedding labour." "Financial market reaction to the labour market deal will be favourable because it should go some way to moderating labour costs. It should be seen as a step in the right direction and possibly as a step that could pave the way to further reform."
DONALD SMITH, INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIST, HSBC LONDON

"They still have a long way to go... We've viewed this generally as a small step moving in the right direction and we're encouraged. Coupled with an impressive performance on inflation and the fiscal deficit this will support market confidence."
JUAN PEREZ CAMPANERO, BANCO SANTANDER, MADRID:
"This is a positive step. However it does not really solve the problems of labour market rigidity."
"It will be partly effective (in preparing the economy for EMU). However it isn't enough, but unions and employers could not go further by themselves."
XAVIER SEGURA PORTA, RESEARCH CHIEF CAJA DE CATALUNYA, BARCELONA:

"I don't think this is going to have a spectacular effect on employment short-term, but if it has a positive effect on temporary work that will be the key success of this agreement. If there is improvement and some temporary contracts become permanent that will provide an important impulse to consumption. The fact that it is something new for companies has to be a favourable contribution."
